title: Where does implement-spec go?
body: Asked again: R2-Q2 came back without an answer. implement-spec builds a whole spec in one run. It reads the tickets as a task graph, starts implementers in their own worktrees across the ready tickets, merges them into one integration branch and finishes with code-review. In AsmAI the Engineering leader already does that with assignments, workspaces, the daemon's fast-forward on acceptance and a handoff to Quality. Only a leader can assign workers, so a worker cannot run it. Options: (A) Shipped as optional and on no list. The Engineering leader's own AsmAI instructions cover working through a ticket graph, assigning each ready ticket to a worker with implement and tdd. (B) On the Engineering leader's list as its method for a ticket graph, mapped by the operating guide. It would be the only skill a leader runs besides Coordination's ask-matt and wait-what.
rec: A. Most of implement-spec describes what AsmAI's daemon and leader contract already do, so running it would be mostly translation. With R2-Q1 A, leaders outside Coordination run no skills.
options: A: optional, on no list; the Engineering leader's own instructions cover ticket graphs
B: on the Engineering leader's list, mapped by the operating guide

title: Which file decides whether a new repository needs setup?
body: Your R2-Q3 note: setup is only required if the repository does not have docs/agent/issue-tracker.md. setup-matt-pocock-skills writes that file as docs/agents/issue-tracker.md (agents, plural), alongside triage-labels.md and domain.md. Options: (A) docs/agents/issue-tracker.md: when you add a repository without it, Coordination opens the setup job; with it, nothing happens, even if the other two files are missing. (B) As A, but also run the setup when triage-labels.md or domain.md is missing.
rec: A, read as the plural folder the skill uses. The issue tracker is the setup the dependent skills cannot work without, and it is what your note named.
options: B: any of the three setup files missing triggers the setup
